sentences.text:
...  Pet  Vs.
 Venkatesan ... Respo
For Petitioner : Ms.G.V.Kasthuri
Additional Public Prosec  ORDER

This Suo Motu Case is dealt with in an extraordinary manner by the Dedicated Bench, pursuant to Suo Motu W.P.(Crl.) No.618 of 2025.
2.This case, Cr.No.24 of 2014 is registered for the alleged offences under Sections 465, 467 468, 471,
420 and 423 IPC.
Upon consideration of the entire case, it can be seen that it is a landlord and tenant dispute.
The parties have moved on and have no objection to the case being disposed of on compromise.

Due to the unique manner in which this designated bench conducts hybrid hearings,
the filing of written affidavits or terms of compromise is dispensed with.
https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis

3.Considering the factual matrix, the context in which the conflict arose, the background of the parties, and their present position, this is an appropriate case for the exercise of jurisdiction under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure as per Gian Singh Vs. State of Punjab and another (2012 10 SCC State Rep. By Inspector Of Police vs Venkatesan on 7 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/38635843/
1 303).
4.Accordingly, the case in C.C.No.43 of 2018 on the file of the Judicial Magistrate Court No.II,
Vellore Taluk, Vellore, stands quashed.

The Trial Court shall take note of the order and accordingly classify the case pending before them as allowed / dismissed / disposed of, etc, and while doing so, consider any applications such as disposal of properties, etc., and pass appropriate orders, as may be necessary.
Further, the Court below is directed to dispatch the copy of this order to all concerned.

D.BHARATHA CHAKRAVARTHY, J.
